dedupe_keys.name: ntp pool project pool ntp org active time servers by zone and their monitoring history

description: The NTP Pool is a large virtual cluster of volunteer time servers that gives Network Time Protocol service to hundreds of millions of systems and is the default time source of most major Linux distributions and many network appliances. On 26 September 2026 the site counted 6,285 active servers: 123 in Africa, 607 in Asia, 3,899 in Europe, 1,312 in North America, 260 in Oceania and 100 in South America, with 3,896 IPv4 and 2,390 IPv6 servers in the global zone. Each continent and country zone page gives the number of active servers now and 1, 7, 14, 60 and 180 days and 1, 3 and 6 years ago, and each server page shows its score from the pool's monitoring over time. Coverage: worldwide, by continent and country zone. Format and access: web pages and per-server score logs, free; the system's source code is public. Caveats: volunteer servers, so coverage is uneven, thin in Africa and South America; counts are of servers, not of clients; monitoring scores reflect the pool's monitors. Simulation uses: the spread and redundancy of internet time sources by country for timing resilience studies, such as losing GNSS-disciplined servers in a region. Related records: data-nist-internet-time-service-servers is a national service; data-bipm-circular-t-utc-time-scale gives the reference time scales.
